instructions: Closed book. For each item: read the stem only and write your solution in stem_only before you read the options. Then choose the answer labels. Use no sources. Set flag to one sentence when you see a second defensible answer or a missing constraint, else null.

items.stem: A company hosts a web application on Amazon EC2 instances. The instances run in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer, and the target group checks the health of the application on each instance. The Auto Scaling group uses only the default Amazon EC2 health checks. Sometimes the web server process on an instance stops after a memory error, the target group marks the instance unhealthy, and the instance still passes its EC2 status checks. The company must ensure that failed instances are replaced automatically. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Leave the health check type of the Auto Scaling group as it is, and rely on the group to replace each instance that it finds unhealthy.

options.label: B
options.text: Install an agent on each instance that tests the web server every minute and reports each failed test to the Auto Scaling API as an unhealthy instance.

options.label: C
options.text: Configure the Application Load Balancer to replace each target that fails its health checks with a new instance from the launch template of the group.

options.label: D
options.text: Set the health check type of the Auto Scaling group to include Elastic Load Balancing, so that the group acts on the health that the target group reports.
